source: DeepSeek platform Usage page (platform.deepseek.com/usage), read from the console
captured: 2026-09-20, range 'Today' in the console's PDT/MST local time, which covers the run
execution: sequential, unbatched, one request in flight
isolation: the day's only DeepSeek activity was this run: 198 requests = 99 x 2 models
note: DeepSeek states usage data is delayed at most 5 minutes, and the run appeared within that window.

caveats.rounding: The console reports whole cents, so a $0.01 figure carries +/- half a cent, i.e. +/- 50 percent.
caveats.off_peak: The run landed on a weekend, and the console states weekends are billed at off-peak rates. These are discounted prices, not standard weekday rates.

peak_rate_source.basis: Off-peak is exactly half of peak for every token category of both models: deepseek-flash cache hit 0.003/0.006, cache miss 0.15/0.30, output 0.60/1.20 per 1M tokens; deepseek-v4-pro cache hit 0.022/0.044, cache miss 0.66/1.32, output 1.98/3.96. Because the discount is uniform across categories, the peak figure is the off-peak figure doubled regardless of the token mix.
peak_rate_source.peak_window: 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. Everything else is off-peak. The run at 04:16 UTC on a Saturday was off-peak on two counts, and that clock hour is outside the peak window on weekdays too.
